Zoe Kim (Stratus): Hi all — onboarding snag. After ~75s of a ramp our API calls toggled to 403 and then a burst of 429s. App logs show 'token_mismatch' then 'quota_exceeded: per_key'. Demo demo next Tue, blocked.
Priya Khatri: Sorry to hear that Zoe. Quick q: which SDK/version and are you routing via a gateway?
Zoe Kim (Stratus): Python SDK v1.3.0 behind our edge-lb which does request multiplexing. We mint ephemeral tokens TTL=110s, refresh 15s before expiry, and keep the previous token for 40s to avoid breaking long requests.
Miguel Ramos: Keeping previous token for 40s could cause overlap if your LB retries/replays headers. Two distinct bearer values within a narrow window can count as separate auth attempts and hit per_key limits.
Avery Long: Can you paste a minimal repro trace or curl example? Even a short header sequence helps.
Zoe Kim (Stratus): Here's from their debug run: ```bash
# initial successful call
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <tokA>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
# ~75s later (swap event)
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <tokA>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat
HTTP/1.1 403 {"error":"token_mismatch","detail":"token_not_recognized"}
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <tokB>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat
HTTP/1.1 429 {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota":"per_key"}
```
Miguel Ramos: Two working hypotheses: 1) LB/clients are replaying old and new headers in flight, doubling auth checks; 2) aggressive local retries after the 403 are immediate and push them over the per-key window. Could also be clock skew making tokens validate unexpectedly.
Priya Khatri: Short mitigation plan: 1) for a quick test, drop the old-token retention to <=5s and add a small jittered backoff on retries (start 100ms). 2) we can enable TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE for Stratus for 90 minutes while you validate. 3) please verify NTP/clock sync across your LBs.
Avery Long: If you canswitch to connection-sticky tokens for streaming flows (keep same token on that connection until it closes) that avoids mid-stream swaps entirely. For request/response, short-old-token is fine.
Zoe Kim (Stratus): Ok doing quick change now: old_keep=3s, backoff=150ms+jitter. Curious: is there a way to see per-session auth counts from your side?
CS Bot: Created ticket CS-12002  labels: onboarding, auth, rate-quota. TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE applied to account stratus-acct until 3432105400. Attached: initial logs from Zoe.
Miguel Ramos: We will attach introspection traces for your key and check for clock skew and revoke events. If none, this strongly points to header replay + retry storm.
Zoe Kim (Stratus): Quick test result: 12m under steady ramp after changes and no 403/429. Good sign. I'll ramp to full load over the next hour.
Priya Khatri: Great. If stable, we'll update the onboarding checklist: - avoid >10s old-token retention behind multiplexing LBs - prefer connection-stickiness for streams - add retry jitter/backoff examples. We'll also add a one-liner reproduce script for support.
Avery Long: Reproduce CLI we recommend to customers: ```bash
# generate tokenA; wait ~85s; generate tokenB; fire both quickly to simulate swap + multiplex
node reproduce-token-swap.js --ttl 110 --swap-before 15 --parallel 2
```
Zoe Kim (Stratus): That reproduce script was helpful. After ramp to prod-level traffic, still clean for 20m. Will report back if anything regresses. Thanks team! :raised_hands:
Priya Khatri: Action items: Zoe to confirm full ramp stable, Miguel to drop introspection notes into CS-12002, Avery to add playbook entry and reproduce snippet to onboarding docs, CS to remove TEMP_PERKEY_GRACE once Zoe confirms. Closing note: this is a common pitfall we should highlight during enablement calls.
